cues.en: Remix,
cues.zh: 混编，

cues.en: to combine or edit existing materials to produce something new.
cues.zh: 就是把现有素材组合或编辑，创造出新东西。

cues.en: The term remix originally applied to music. It rose to prominence late last century during the heyday of hip hop, the first popular music form to incorporate sampling from existing recordings.
cues.zh: “混编”一词最早用于音乐。上世纪后期嘻哈音乐鼎盛时期它开始走红，嘻哈是第一种大量采样现有录音的流行音乐形式。

cues.en: Early
cues.zh: 早期

cues.en: example, Sugarhill gang samples the bass riff from Sheik's Good Times in the 1979 hit Rapper's Delight.
cues.zh: 例子，Sugarhill Gang 在1979年的热门歌曲 Rapper's Delight 中采样了 Chic 的 Good Times 的贝斯 riff。

cues.en: Skip ahead to the present and anybody can remix anything, music, video, photos, whatever, and distribute it globally pretty much instantly. You don't need expensive tools. You don't need a distributor. You don't even need skills.
cues.zh: 快进到今天，任何人都能混编任何东西——音乐、视频、照片，什么都可以，而且几乎能瞬间全球发布。你不需要昂贵的工具。不需要发行商。甚至不需要专业技能。

cues.en: Remixing is a folk art. Anybody can do it. Yet these techniques, collecting material, combining it, transforming it, are the same ones used at any level of creation. You could even say that everything is a remix.
cues.zh: 混音是一种民间艺术，人人都能玩。但收集素材、整合并改造这些技术，贯穿了所有层面的创作。你甚至可以说，万物皆混音。

cues.en: To explain, let's start in England in 1968.
cues.zh: 为了解释清楚，我们回到 1968 年的英格兰。

cues.en: Jimmy Page recruits John Paul Jones, Robert Plant, and and John Bonham to form Led Zeppelin.
cues.zh: Jimmy Page 招募了 John Paul Jones、Robert Plant 和 John Bonham，组成了 Led Zeppelin 乐队。

cues.en: They play extremely loud blues music that will soon be known as,
cues.zh: 他们演奏着声音极大的蓝调音乐，这种风格很快就被称为……

cues.en: wait.
cues.zh: 等等。

cues.en: Let's start in Paris in 1961.
cues.zh: 我们从1961年的巴黎说起。

cues.en: William Burroughs coins the term heavy metal in the novel The Soft Machine, a book composed using the cut up technique, taking existing writing and literally chopping it up and rearranging it. So in 1961,
cues.zh: William Burroughs 在小说《软机器》中创造了“重金属”一词，这本书采用剪裁技法，把现有文字剪碎再重新排列。所以在1961年，

cues.en: William Burroughs not only invents the term heavy metal, the brand of music Zeppelin and a few other groups of Pioneer, he also produces an early remix.
cues.zh: William Burroughs 不仅发明了“重金属”这个词，也就是 Led Zeppelin 和另外几支先驱乐队的音乐风格，他还做出了早期的混音作品。

cues.en: Back to Zeppelin. By the mid nineteen seventies, Led Zeppelin are the biggest touring rock band in America, yet many critics and peers label them as
cues.zh: 回到 Led Zeppelin。到七十年代中期，Led Zeppelin 已是美国巡演规模最大的摇滚乐队，但许多评论家和同行却给他们贴上

cues.en: rip offs. The case goes like this. The opening and closing sections of Bring It On Home are lifted from a tune by Willie Dixon entitled, not coincidentally, Bring It On Home. The
cues.zh: 抄袭的标签。事情是这样的。《Bring It On Home》的开头和结尾部分取自 Willie Dixon 的一首曲子，歌名恰巧也叫《Bring It On Home》。

cues.en: Lemon song lifts numerous lyrics from Helen Wolf's Killing Floor.
cues.zh: 《The Lemon Song》从 Helen Wolf 的《Killing Floor》里挪用了大量歌词。

cues.en: Black Mountainside lifts its melody from Black Waterside, a traditional arranged by Bert Janch.
cues.zh: 《Black Mountain Side》的旋律借鉴了传统民谣《Black Waterside》，由 Bert Jansch 改编。

cues.en: Dazed and Confused features different lyrics but is clearly an uncredited cover of the same title song by Jake Holmes. Oddly enough, Holmes filed suit over forty years later in 2010.
cues.zh: 《Dazed and Confused》虽然改了歌词，但显然翻唱自 Jake Holmes 的同名歌曲，且未署名。奇怪的是，Holmes 直到四十多年后的 2010 年才提起诉讼。

cues.en: And the big one, Stairway to Heaven pulls its opening from Spirit's Taurus. Zeppelin toured with Spirit in 1968,
cues.zh: 最著名的那首《Stairway to Heaven》，其前奏取材自 Spirit 乐队的《Taurus》。齐柏林飞艇（Led Zeppelin）曾在 1968 年与 Spirit 一同巡演，

cues.en: three years before Stairway was released.
cues.zh: 那是《Stairway to Heaven》发行的三年前。

cues.en: Zeppelin clearly copied a lot of other people's material,
cues.zh: Zeppelin显然抄袭了许多他人的作品，

cues.en: but that alone isn't unusual. Only two things distinguish Zeppelin from their peers. Firstly, when Zeppelin used someone else's material, they didn't attribute songwriting to the original artist. Most British blues groups were recording lots of covers, but unlike Zeppelin, they didn't claim to have written them. Secondly, Zeppelin didn't modify their versions enough to claim they were original. Many bands knock off acts that came before them, but they tend to emulate the general sound rather than specific lyrics or melodies.
cues.zh: 但单凭这一点并不罕见。只有两点让Zeppelin区别于同行。第一，当Zeppelin使用他人作品时，他们没有把创作署名归于原创艺术家。大多数英国布鲁斯乐队都在录制大量翻唱，但与Zeppelin不同，他们并未声称这些歌是自己写的。第二，Zeppelin对他们版本的改动不够大，不足以声称它们是原创。许多乐队都会模仿前辈的表演，但他们往往效仿整体风格，而非具体的歌词或旋律。

cues.en: Zeppelin copied without making fundamental changes.
cues.zh: Zeppelin 几乎原封不动地照搬了过来。

cues.en: So these two things, covers, performances of other people's material, and knockoffs,
cues.zh: 所以翻唱（演绎他人的作品）和仿制，

cues.en: copies that stay within legal boundaries,
cues.zh: 也就是在法律允许范围内的模仿，

cues.en: these are long standing examples of legal remixing.
cues.zh: 都是长期以来合法的“混音再创作”范例。

cues.en: This stuff accounts for almost everything the entertainment industry produces,
cues.zh: 这类创作几乎占据了娱乐产业产出的全部，

cues.en: and that's where we're headed in part two.
cues.zh: 而这正是我们第二部分要讲的内容。

cues.en: Wait. One last thing. In the wake of their enormous success, Led Zeppelin went from the copier to the copied.
cues.zh: 等等，还有最后一件事。随着巨大的成功，Led Zeppelin 从抄袭者变成了被抄袭的对象。

cues.en: First in the seventies with groups like Aerosmith and Hart and Boston, then during the eighties heavy metal craze and on into the era of sampling.
cues.zh: 最早是七十年代，像Aerosmith、Hart和Boston这样的乐队，然后是八十年代的重金属热潮，接着进入采样时代。

cues.en: Here's the beats from When the Levee Breaks getting sampled and remixed.
cues.zh: 这是《When the Levee Breaks》的节拍被采样和重新混音的效果。

cues.en: In Zeppelin's defense, they never sued anybody.
cues.zh: 替Led Zeppelin说句公道话，他们从没起诉过任何人。

cues.en: Perhaps
cues.zh: 也许

cues.en: it's because movies are so massively expensive to make. Perhaps it's because graphic novels, TV shows, video games, books, and the like are such rich sources of material,
cues.zh: 是因为电影制作成本太高了。也许是因为图像小说、电视节目、电子游戏、书籍之类的素材来源太丰富了，

cues.en: or perhaps it's because audiences just prefer the familiar.
cues.zh: 又或者是因为观众就是偏爱熟悉的东西。

cues.en: Whatever the reason, most box office hits rely heavily on existing material.
cues.zh: 不管出于什么原因，大多数票房大片都极度依赖现有素材。

cues.en: Of the 10 highest grossing films per year from the last ten years,
cues.zh: 在过去十年中，每年的票房前十名里，

cues.en: 74 out of 100
cues.zh: 这100部电影中有74部，

cues.en: are either sequels or remakes of earlier films or adaptations of comic books, video games, books, and so on.
cues.zh: 要么是早期电影的续集或翻拍，要么改编自漫画、电子游戏、书籍等。

cues.en: Transforming the old into the new is Hollywood's
cues.zh: 将旧内容改头换面、推陈出新，是好莱坞

cues.en: greatest talent.
cues.zh: 最大的本事。

cues.en: At this point, we've got three sequels to a film adapted from a theme park attraction.
cues.zh: 到了今天，我们甚至能看到一部改编自主题公园游乐项目的电影，一口气拍了三部续集。

cues.en: We've got a movie musical based on a musical, which was based on a movie. We've
cues.zh: 我们有一部音乐电影，改编自一部音乐剧，而那部音乐剧又改编自一部电影。我们还

cues.en: got two sequels to a film that was adapted from an animated TV show based on a line of toys.
cues.zh: 有两部续集，原片改编自动画电视剧，而那部动画剧又源自一系列玩具。

cues.en: We've
cues.zh: 我们还

cues.en: got a movie based on two books, one of which was based on a blog, which was inspired by the other book that was adapted into the film. Julie and Julia. Do you follow? We've got 11 Star Trek films, 12 Friday the thirteenth, and 23
cues.zh: 有一部电影改编自两本书，其中一本基于一个博客，而这个博客的灵感来源于另一本书，那本书又被改编成了这部电影。《朱莉与朱莉娅》。你听明白了吗？我们有11部《星际迷航》电影，12部《十三号星期五》，还有23部

cues.en: James Bonds. We've
cues.zh: 詹姆斯·邦德电影。我们

cues.en: got stories that have been told, retold, transformed, referenced, and subverted since the dawn of cinema.
cues.zh: 有自电影诞生以来被讲述、重述、改编、引用和颠覆的故事。

cues.en: We've seen vampires morph from hideous monsters to caped bedroom invaders to campy jokes to sexy hunks
cues.zh: 我们见证了吸血鬼从可怕的怪物，变成披着斗篷夜闯卧室的魅影，再变成滑稽的笑料，最后成了性感帅哥，

cues.en: to sexier hunks.
cues.zh: 甚至是更性感的猛男。

cues.en: Of the few box office hits that aren't sequels,
cues.zh: 在少数几部非续集的票房大作中，

cues.en: remakes, or adaptations,
cues.zh: 它们既不是翻拍，也不是改编，

cues.en: the word original
cues.zh: 但用“原创”这个词

cues.en: wouldn't spring to mind to describe them. These are genre movies and they stick to pretty standard templates.
cues.zh: 来形容它们也并不贴切。这些都是类型片，而且严格遵循相当标准的套路。

cues.en: Genres then break up into subgenres with their own even more specific conventions.
cues.zh: 类型又进一步细分为子类型，拥有更加具体的惯用套路。

cues.en: So within the category of horror films, we have subgenres like slasher,
cues.zh: 比如在恐怖片这个大类下，我们有砍杀片、

cues.en: zombie, creature feature, and of course, torture porn.
cues.zh: 丧尸片、怪兽片等子类型，当然，还有虐杀片。

cues.en: All have standard elements that are appropriated,
cues.zh: 它们都有可被挪用的标准元素，

cues.en: transformed,
cues.zh: 被改造，

cues.en: and subverted.
cues.zh: 并被颠覆。

cues.en: Let's use the biggest film of the decade as an example.
cues.zh: 让我们以这十年最火的电影为例。

cues.en: Now it's not a sequel, remake, or adaptation,
cues.zh: 它不是续集、翻拍或改编，

cues.en: but it is a genre film, sci fi, and most tellingly, it's a member of a tiny subgenre where sympathetic white people feel bad about all the murder, pillaging, and annihilation being done on their behalf.
cues.zh: 但它是一部类型片，科幻片，最能说明问题的是，它属于一个极小的子类型——在这个子类型中，有同情心的白人对自己以他们的名义所进行的杀戮、掠夺和毁灭感到难过。

cues.en: I call this subgenre sorry about colonialism.
cues.zh: 我把这个子类型称为“对殖民主义感到抱歉”。

cues.en: I'm talking about movies like dances with wolves, the last samurai, the last of the Mohicans, dune, Lawrence of Arabia, A Man Called Horse, and even Fern Gully and Pocahontas.
cues.zh: 我说的是像《与狼共舞》、《最后的武士》、《最后的莫希干人》、《沙丘》、《阿拉伯的劳伦斯》、《一个叫马的男人》，甚至是《辛巴达历险记》和《风中奇缘》这样的电影。

cues.en: Films
cues.zh: 电影

cues.en: are built on other films as well as on books, TV shows, actual events, plays, whatever. This applies to everything from the lowliest genre film right on up to revered indie fare. And it even applies to massively influential
cues.zh: 是建立在其他电影之上的，同时也借鉴了书籍、电视节目、真实事件、戏剧等等。从最底层的类型片，一直到备受推崇的独立佳作，无一例外。这甚至也适用于那些影响深远的

cues.en: blockbusters,
cues.zh: 商业大片，

cues.en: the kinds of films that reshape pop culture,
cues.zh: 就是那些重塑了流行文化的电影，

cues.en: which brings us to...
cues.zh: 这就引出了……

cues.en: Even now, Star Wars endures as a work of impressive imagination,
cues.zh: 即使在今天，《星球大战》仍是一部想象力惊人的作品，

cues.en: but many of its individual components are as recognizable as the samples in a remix.
cues.zh: 但它的许多单个组成部分就像混音中的采样一样耳熟能详。

cues.en: The foundation for Star Wars comes from Joseph Campbell.
cues.zh: 《星球大战》的基础来自约瑟夫·坎贝尔。

cues.en: He popularized the structures of myth in his book, The Hero with a Thousand Faces.
cues.zh: 他在《千面英雄》一书中普及了神话的结构。

cues.en: Star Wars follows the outline of the monomyth,
cues.zh: 《星球大战》遵循单一神话的框架，

cues.en: which consists of stages like the call to adventure, supernatural aid, the belly of the whale, the road of trials, the meeting with the goddess, and a bunch more.
cues.zh: 其中包括冒险的召唤、超自然的援助、鲸鱼之腹、试炼之路、与女神的相遇等许多阶段。

cues.en: Also huge influences were the Flash Gordon serials from the thirties and Japanese director Akira Kurosawa.
cues.zh: 同样产生巨大影响的，还有30年代的《飞天红侠》（Flash Gordon）系列短片和日本导演黑泽明。

cues.en: Star Wars plays much like an updated version of Flash Gordon, right down to the softwipes and the opening title's design.
cues.zh: 《星球大战》看起来很像《飞天红侠》的升级版，连软划变焦转场和片头字幕设计都如出一辙。

cues.en: From Kurosawa, we get masters of spiritual martial arts, a low ranking bickering duo, more softwipes,
cues.zh: 而从黑泽明那里，我们看到了精神武术大师、地位低下且爱拌嘴的二人组、更多的软划变焦转场、

cues.en: a beneath the floorboards hideaway, and a boastful baddie getting his arm chopped off. You
cues.zh: 地板下的藏身处，还有一个自吹自擂的反派被砍掉了手臂。你

cues.en: just watch yourself. We want it in. I have the death sentence on 12 systems.
cues.zh: 最好小心点。我们被通缉了。我在12个星系都被判了死刑。

cues.en: War films and westerns were also huge sources for Star Wars. The scene where Luke discovers his slaughtered family resembles this scene from the searchers.
cues.zh: 战争片和西部片也是《星球大战》的重要灵感来源。卢克发现家人被屠杀的那场戏，就类似《搜索者》中的这一幕。

cues.en: And the scene where Han Solo shoots Greedo
cues.zh: 而汉·索罗开枪打格雷多那场戏

cues.en: resembles this scene from the good, the bad, and the ugly.
cues.zh: 则类似《黄金三镖客》中的这一幕。

cues.en: The climactic airstrikes in the dambusters,
cues.zh: 《炸坝者》中高潮部分的空袭、

cues.en: six three three squadron, and the bridges at Toko Ri play very similarly to the run-in the Death Star. And in many cases, existing shots were even used as templates for Star Wars special effects.
cues.zh: 《633轰炸大队》以及《东京暗礁桥》的空战，其运镜方式和进攻死星非常相似。很多情况下，现成的镜头甚至被直接当作《星球大战》特效的模板。

cues.en: I
cues.zh: 我

cues.en: got him. Bring him. Don't get cocky. There's also many other elements clearly derived from various films. We have a tin man like the tin woman in Metropolis,
cues.zh: 抓到他了。带他过来。别得意。还有许多元素显然借鉴了各类电影。比如一个像《大都会》（Metropolis）中机器女人的锡人，

cues.en: a couple shots inspired by 2001,
cues.zh: 几个受《2001太空漫游》（2001: A Space Odyssey）启发的镜头，

cues.en: a grab the girl in swing scene like this one in the seventh voyage of Sinbad, a holographic projection kinda like the one in Forbidden Planet, a rally resembling this one in Triumph of the Will, and cute little robots much like those in Silent Running.
cues.zh: 一个类似于《辛巴达第七次航行》（The 7th Voyage of Sinbad）里抱起女孩荡秋千的场景，一个有点像《禁忌星球》（Forbidden Planet）里的全息投影，一场类似于《意志的胜利》（Triumph of the Will）的集会，以及和《宇宙静悄悄》（Silent Running）里非常相似的可爱小机器人。

cues.en: George Lucas collected materials. He combined them. He transformed them. Without the films that preceded it, there could be no Star Wars. Creation requires influence.
cues.zh: George Lucas 收集素材，加以组合，进行转化。没有此前的那些电影，就不会有《星球大战》。创作需要影响。

cues.en: Everything we make is a remix of existing creations,
cues.zh: 我们创造的一切，都是对既有作品的重新混编，

cues.en: our lives, and the lives of others. As Isaac Newton once said, we stand on the shoulders of giants,
cues.zh: 包括我们的生活，以及他人的生活。正如 Isaac Newton 曾说，我们站在巨人的肩膀上，

cues.en: which is what he was doing when he adapted that saying from Bernard de Chartres. In part three, we'll further explore this idea and chart the blurry boundary between the original and the unoriginal.
cues.zh: 而他这句话正是改编自 Bernard de Chartres 的说法。在第三部分，我们将进一步探讨这一理念，并勾勒原创与非原创之间那模糊的边界。

cues.en: George Lucas was the most movie saturated filmmaker of his era, but that baton has since been passed to...
cues.zh: 乔治·卢卡斯曾是那个时代阅片量最庞大的电影人，但接力棒如今已经交到了……

cues.en: Quentin Tarantino's remix master thesis is kill bill, which is probably the closest thing Hollywood has to a mash up.
cues.zh: 昆汀·塔伦蒂诺的混剪集大成之作是《杀死比尔》，这大概是好莱坞最接近 Mashup 风格的作品了。

cues.en: Packed with elements pulled from countless films,
cues.zh: 它融合了从无数电影中汲取的元素，

cues.en: Kill Bill raises filmic sampling to new heights of sophistication.
cues.zh: 《杀死比尔》将电影层面的“采样”推向了精妙绝伦的新高度。

cues.en: The killer nurse scene in particular is almost entirely a recombination of elements from existing films.
cues.zh: 尤其是那个杀手护士的桥段，几乎完全是由已有电影的元素重新拼贴而成的。

cues.en: The basic action is the same as this scene from Black Sunday, where a woman disguised as a nurse attempts to murder a patient with a syringe of red fluid.
cues.zh: 基本动作和《黑色星期天》里的这一幕相同，片中一名伪装成护士的女子试图用一针管红色液体谋杀一名病人。

cues.en: Daryl Hannah's eye patch is a nod to the lead character in They Call Her One Eye, and the tune she's whistling is taken from the 1968 thriller Twisted Nerve.... See you this evening. No. No. It's for you, Todd. Hold tight.
cues.zh: Daryl Hannah 的眼罩是在致敬《他们叫她独眼》的主角，她吹的曲调取自1968年的惊悚片《扭曲的神经》……今晚见。不。不。是找你的，Todd。别挂。

cues.en: Capping it off, the split screen effect is modeled on techniques used by Brian DePalma in an assortment of films, including Carrie.
cues.zh: 最后，分屏效果是仿照 Brian DePalma 在多部电影中使用的技巧，包括《魔女嘉莉》。

cues.en: For an extended look at Kill Bill's references, check this out.
cues.zh: 想深入了解《Kill Bill》中的各种致敬，可以看看这个。

cues.en: The act of creation is surrounded by a fog of myths.
cues.zh: 创造这一行为，一直被重重迷思所笼罩。

cues.en: Myths that creativity comes via inspiration,
cues.zh: 比如认为创造力全凭灵光一闪，

cues.en: that original creations break the mold, that they're the products of geniuses,
cues.zh: 认为原创作品打破常规、是天才的产物，

cues.en: and appear as quickly as electricity can heat a filament.
cues.zh: 诞生得就像通电点亮灯丝一样迅速。

cues.en: But creativity
cues.zh: 但创造力

cues.en: isn't magic.
cues.zh: 并不是魔法。

cues.en: It happens by applying ordinary tools of thought to existing materials.
cues.zh: 它是将普通的思维工具，应用在已有素材上的结果。

cues.en: And the soil from which we grow our creations is something we scorn and misunderstand
cues.zh: 而孕育我们创作成品的土壤，却往往被我们鄙视和误解，

cues.en: even though it gives us so much,
cues.zh: 哪怕它带给了我们如此多的滋养，

cues.en: and that's
cues.zh: 那就是——

cues.en: copying.
cues.zh: 复制。

cues.en: Put simply, copying is how we learn. We can't introduce anything new until we're fluent in the language of our domain, and we do that through emulation.
cues.zh: 简单说，模仿就是我们的学习方式。只有熟练掌握了所在领域的语言，我们才能引入新东西，而这要靠模仿来实现。

cues.en: For instance, all artists spend their formative years producing derivative work.
cues.zh: 比如，所有艺术家在成长阶段都在创作衍生作品。

cues.en: Bob Dylan's first album contained 11 cover songs.
cues.zh: Bob Dylan 的第一张专辑里有 11 首翻唱歌曲。

cues.en: Richard Pryor began his stand up career doing a not very good imitation of Bill Cosby,
cues.zh: Richard Pryor 刚开始讲脱口秀时，是在模仿 Bill Cosby，还模仿得不怎么样，

cues.en: And Hunter s Thompson retyped The Great Gatsby just to get the feel of writing a great novel.
cues.zh: Hunter S. Thompson 把《了不起的盖茨比》重新打了一遍，只为体会写出一部伟大长篇小说的感觉。

cues.en: Nobody starts out original. We need copying to build a foundation of knowledge and understanding.
cues.zh: 没有人一开始就具备原创能力，我们需要通过模仿来打下知识和理解的基石。

cues.en: And after that,
cues.zh: 在此之后，

cues.en: things can get interesting.
cues.zh: 事情才会变得有趣起来。

cues.en: After we've grounded ourselves in the fundamentals through copying, it's then possible to create something new through transformation,
cues.zh: 当我们通过模仿打牢基础后，才有可能通过转化来创造新事物，

cues.en: taking an idea and creating variations.
cues.zh: 也就是借鉴某个想法，并不断做出演化改动。

cues.en: This is time consuming tinkering, but it can eventually produce a breakthrough.
cues.zh: 这种摸索非常耗费时间，但最终可能带来突破。

cues.en: James Watt created a major improvement to the steam engine because he was assigned to repair a Thomas Newcomen steam engine. He then spent twelve years developing his version. Christopher Latham Scholes modeled his typewriter keyboard on a piano. This design slowly evolved over five years into the QWERTY layout we still use today. And Thomas Edison didn't invent the light bulb. His first patent was improvement in electric lamps, but he did produce the first commercially viable one after trying 6,000
cues.zh: 詹姆斯·瓦特之所以对蒸汽机做出了重大改进，是因为他当时接到了修理纽科门蒸汽机的任务，随后他花了十二年时间研发出自己的版本；克里斯托弗·拉瑟姆·肖尔斯以钢琴为原型设计了打字机键盘，经过五年的缓慢演变，最终变成了我们今天仍在使用的 QWERTY 布局；而托马斯·爱迪生并没有发明电灯泡，他的第一项专利只是对电灯的改进，但他确实在尝试了6000种

cues.en: different materials for the filament.
cues.zh: 灯丝可以用不同的材料。

cues.en: These are all major advances, but they're not original ideas so much as tipping points in a continuous line of invention by many different people.
cues.zh: 这些都是重大进步，但它们与其说是原创想法，不如说是许多人持续发明过程中的临界点。

cues.en: But the most dramatic results can happen when ideas are combined.
cues.zh: 但当想法结合在一起时，最惊人的结果可能就会发生。

cues.en: By connecting ideas together, creative leaps can be made, producing some of history's
cues.zh: 通过将想法连接起来，可以实现创造性的飞跃，产生历史上一些

cues.en: biggest breakthroughs.
cues.zh: 最大的突破。

cues.en: Johann Gutenberg's printing press was invented around 1440,
cues.zh: Johann Gutenberg的印刷机发明于1440年左右，

cues.en: but almost all its components had been around for centuries.
cues.zh: 但几乎所有的部件都已经存在了几个世纪。

cues.en: Henry Ford and the Ford Motor Company didn't invent the assembly line, interchangeable parts, or even the automobile itself, but they combined all these elements in nineteen o eight to produce the first mass market car, the Model t. And the Internet slowly grew over several decades as as networks and protocols merged. It finally hit critical mass in 1991
cues.zh: 亨利·福特和福特汽车公司并没有发明装配线、可互换零部件，甚至也没发明汽车本身，但他们在 1908 年将所有这些元素结合在一起，制造出了第一款大众市场汽车——Model T。互联网也是在几十年间随着网络和协议的融合而缓慢发展的，最终在 1991 年迎来了爆发的临界点，

cues.en: when Tim Berners Lee added the World Wide Web.
cues.zh: 当时蒂姆·伯纳斯-李（Tim Berners-Lee）推出了万维网（World Wide Web）。

cues.en: These are the basic elements of creativity.
cues.zh: 这些是创造力的基本要素。

cues.en: Copy,
cues.zh: 复制，

cues.en: transform,
cues.zh: 转换，

cues.en: and combine.
cues.zh: 再组合。

cues.en: And the perfect illustration of all these at work is the story of the devices we're using right now. So let's travel back to the dawn of the personal computer revolution
cues.zh: 而这一切发挥作用的最佳例证，就是我们此刻正在使用的设备的故事。让我们回到个人电脑革命的开端，

cues.en: and look at the company that started it all.
cues.zh: 看看开创这一切的那家公司。

cues.en: Xerox.
cues.zh: 施乐。

cues.en: Xerox invented the modern personal computer in the early seventies.
cues.zh: 施乐在七十年代初发明了现代个人电脑。

cues.en: The Alto was a mouse driven system with a graphical user interface.
cues.zh: Alto 是一套鼠标驱动的系统，配有图形用户界面。

cues.en: Bear in mind that a popular personal computer of this era was operated with switches,
cues.zh: 要知道，那个年代流行的个人电脑还是靠拨动开关来操作的，

cues.en: and if you flip them in the right order, you got to see blinking lights.
cues.zh: 只要按正确的顺序拨动开关，就能看到指示灯闪烁。

cues.en: The Alto was way ahead of its time.
cues.zh: Alto 远远超越了它所处的时代。

cues.en: Eventually, Apple got a load of the Alto and later released not one, but two computers with graphical interfaces, the Lisa and its more successful follow-up, the Macintosh.
cues.zh: 最终，Apple 见识到了 Alto，后来不仅推出了一款，而是两款带图形界面的电脑：Lisa 和后来更成功的 Macintosh。

cues.en: The Alto was never a commercial product, but Xerox did release a system based on it in 1981,
cues.zh: Alto 从未作为商业产品发售，但 Xerox 确实在 1981 年发布了一款基于它的系统，

cues.en: the Star 8010,
cues.zh: 那就是 Star 8010，

cues.en: two years before the Lisa, three years before the Mac. It was the star on the Alto that served as the foundation for the Macintosh.
cues.zh: 比 Lisa 早了两年，比 Mac 早了三年。正是 Alto 上的 Star，奠定了 Macintosh 的基石。

cues.en: The Xerox Star used a desktop metaphor with icons for documents and folders.
cues.zh: Xerox Star 采用了桌面隐喻，用图标表示文档和文件夹。

cues.en: It had a pointer, scroll bars, and pop up menus.
cues.zh: 它有指针、滚动条和弹出菜单。

cues.en: These were huge innovations and the Mac copied every one of them. But it was the first combination it incorporated that set the Mac on a path towards long term success.
cues.zh: 这些都是巨大的创新，Mac 全都照搬了。但正是它整合的第一个组合，让 Mac 走上了长期成功的道路。

cues.en: Apple aimed to merge the computer with the household appliance.
cues.zh: Apple 的目标是让计算机与家用电器融为一体。

cues.en: The Mac was to be a simple device like a TV or a stereo.
cues.zh: Mac 要成为像电视或音响那样简单的设备。

cues.en: This was unlike the Star, which was intended for professional use and vastly different from the cumbersome command based systems that dominated the era. The Mac was for the home and this produced a cascade of transformations.
cues.zh: 这与面向专业用途的 Star 完全不同，也彻底告别了那个时代主流的繁琐命令行系统。Mac 是面向家庭的，这引发了一连串的变革。

cues.en: Firstly, Apple removed one of the buttons on the mouse to make its novel pointing device less confusing.
cues.zh: 首先，Apple 去掉了鼠标上的一个按键，让这个新颖的指针设备用起来不那么让人困惑。

cues.en: Then they added the double click for opening files. The star used a separate key to open files. The Mac also let you drag icons around and move and resize windows. The star didn't have drag and drop. You moved and copied files by selecting an icon, pressing a key, then clicking a location, and your resized windows with a menu. The star and the Alto both featured pop up menus, but because the location of these would move around the screen, the user had to continually reorient.
cues.zh: 接着，他们加入了双击打开文件的操作。而 Star 则是用一个单独的按键来打开文件。Mac 还支持拖拽图标，以及移动和调整窗口大小。Star 并不支持拖放，移动和复制文件得先选定图标、按下一个键，然后再点击目标位置，调整窗口大小也得通过菜单。Star 和 Alto 虽然都有弹出菜单，但因为菜单弹出的位置会在屏幕上到处变，用户就不得不频繁重新定位视线。

cues.en: The Mac introduced the menu bar, which stayed in the same place no matter what you were doing. And the Mac added the trash can to make deleting files more intuitive and less nerve racking.
cues.zh: Mac 引入了菜单栏，无论你在做什么，它都始终停在同一个地方。Mac 还加入了废纸篓，让删除文件更直观、也没那么令人紧张。

cues.en: And lastly, through compromise and clever engineering,
cues.zh: 最后，通过折中和巧妙的工程设计，

cues.en: Apple managed to pair the Mac's price down to $2,500.
cues.zh: Apple 成功把 Mac 的价格压到了 2500 美元。

cues.en: Still pretty expensive, but much cheaper than the $10,000
cues.zh: 还是挺贵，但比 1 万美元的

cues.en: Lisa or the $17,000
cues.zh: Lisa 或 1.7 万美元的

cues.en: Star.
cues.zh: Star 便宜多了。

cues.en: But what started it all was the graphical interface merged with the idea of the computer as household appliance.
cues.zh: 但这一切的起点，是图形界面，加上把电脑当作家用电器这个理念的结合。

cues.en: The Mac is a demonstration of the explosive potential of combinations.
cues.zh: Mac 展现了技术组合所带来的爆发性潜力。

cues.en: The star and the Alto, on the other hand, are the products of years of elite research and development.
cues.zh: 而 Star 和 Alto 则是多年顶尖研发的结晶。

cues.en: They're a testament to the slow power of transformation.
cues.zh: 它们证明了渐进式变革所蕴含的深厚力量。

cues.en: But, of course, they too contain the work of others. The Alto and the Star are evolutionary branches that lead back to the NLS system, which introduced Windows and the mouse, to Sketchpad, the first interactive drawing application,
cues.zh: 当然，它们同样凝聚了他人的心血。Alto 和 Star 都是进化树上的分支，可以一路追溯到开创了窗口和鼠标的 NLS 系统，追溯到首个交互式绘图应用 Sketchpad，

cues.en: and even back to the Memex, a concept resembling the modern PC
cues.zh: 甚至能追溯到 Memex，一个类似现代 PC 的构想，

cues.en: decades before it was possible.
cues.zh: 而在当时，距离它的实现还有几十年之久。

cues.en: The interdependence
cues.zh: 相互依存

cues.en: of our creativity has been obscured by powerful cultural ideas,
cues.zh: 我们的创造力之间的相互联系被强大的文化观念所掩盖，

cues.en: but technology is now exposing this connectedness.
cues.zh: 但技术现在正揭示这种连通性。

cues.en: We're struggling legally, ethically, and artistically
cues.zh: 我们在法律、伦理和艺术上都在努力

cues.en: to deal with these implications,
cues.zh: 应对这些影响，

cues.en: And that's our final episode,
cues.zh: 这是我们的最后一集，

cues.en: part four.
cues.zh: 第四部分。

cues.en: What if Xerox never decided to pursue the graphical interface
cues.zh: 如果施乐从未决定追求图形界面

cues.en: or Thomas Edison found a different trade?
cues.zh: 或者托马斯·爱迪生从事了不同的行业呢？

cues.en: What if Tim Berners Lee never got the funding to develop the World Wide Web? Would our world be different?
cues.zh: 如果蒂姆·伯纳斯-李从未获得开发万维网的资金呢？我们的世界会有所不同吗？

cues.en: Would we be further behind?
cues.zh: 我们会落后更多吗？

cues.en: History seems to tell us things wouldn't be so different.
cues.zh: 历史似乎告诉我们，情况并不会有什么不同。

cues.en: Whenever there's a major breakthrough, there's usually others on the same path. Maybe a bit behind, maybe not behind at all.
cues.zh: 每当出现重大突破时，通常都有其他人在同一条路上探索。也许落后一点，也许根本没落后。

cues.en: Isaac Newton and Godfrey Leibniz both invented calculus around 1684.
cues.zh: Isaac Newton 和 Gottfried Leibniz 都在 1684 年左右发明了微积分。

cues.en: Charles Darwin proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection, but Alfred Russel Wallace had pretty much the same idea at pretty much the same time.
cues.zh: Charles Darwin 提出了自然选择的进化论，但 Alfred Russel Wallace 几乎在同一时间也有了完全相同的想法。

cues.en: And Alexander Graham Bell and Elisha Gray filed patents for the telephone on the same day.
cues.zh: 亚历山大·格拉汉姆·贝尔和伊莱沙·格雷在同一天为电话申请了专利。

cues.en: We call this a multiple discovery,
cues.zh: 我们称之为多重发现，

cues.en: the same innovation emerging from different places.
cues.zh: 同一项创新从不同地方涌现。

cues.en: Science and invention is riddled with it, but it can also happen in the arts.
cues.zh: 科学和发明中比比皆是，但艺术领域也会发生。

cues.en: In film, for instance, we had three Coco Chanel movies released within nine months of each other. Around 1999,
cues.zh: 比如电影界，我们有三个可可·香奈儿电影在九个月内相继上映。大约1999年，

cues.en: we had a quartet of sci fi movies about artificial reality.
cues.zh: 我们有四部关于人工现实的科幻电影。

cues.en: Even Charlie Kaufman's unusually original film Synecdoche, New York bears an uncanny resemblance to Tom McCarthy's novel Remainder.
cues.zh: 就连 Charlie Kaufman 极其原创的电影《纽约提纲》，也与 Tom McCarthy 的小说《Remainder》惊人地相似。

cues.en: Both are the stories of men who suddenly become wealthy and start recreating moments of their lives, even going so far as to recreate
cues.zh: 两部作品讲的都是主人公突然暴富，开始重现自己生活中的种种片段，甚至不惜去重现

cues.en: the recreations.
cues.zh: 那些“被重现出来的场景”。

cues.en: And actually, this, the video you're watching, was written just before the New Yorker published a Malcolm Gladwell story about Apple, Xerox, and the nature of innovation.
cues.zh: 事实上，你正在看的这个视频脚本，刚写完不久，《纽约客》就发表了 Malcolm Gladwell 撰写的一篇关于 Apple、Xerox 以及创新本质的文章。

cues.en: We're all building with the same materials.
cues.zh: 我们都在用同样的材料构建。

cues.en: Sometimes by coincidence, we get similar results, but sometimes innovations
cues.zh: 有时出于巧合，我们会得到相似的结果，但有时创新

cues.en: just seem inevitable.
cues.zh: 似乎就是不可避免的。

cues.en: The genes in our bodies can be traced back over 3,500,000,000
cues.zh: 我们体内的基因可以追溯到35亿年前

cues.en: to a single organism,
cues.zh: 到一个单一生物体，

cues.en: Luca, the last universal
cues.zh: Luca，最后的普遍

cues.en: common
cues.zh: 共同

cues.en: ancestor.
cues.zh: 祖先。

cues.en: As Luca reproduced, its genes copied and copied and copied and copied.
cues.zh: 随着Luca繁殖，它的基因不断复制、复制、复制、复制。

cues.en: Sometimes with mistakes,
cues.zh: 有时会出错，

cues.en: they transformed.
cues.zh: 它们就发生了转变。

cues.en: Over time, this produced every one of the billions of species of life on earth. Some of these adopted sexual reproduction
cues.zh: 随着时间推移，这产生了地球上数十亿种生命中的每一种。其中一些采用了有性繁殖

cues.en: combining the genes of individuals,
cues.zh: 结合个体的基因，

cues.en: and altogether, the best adapted life forms prospered.
cues.zh: 总的来说，最适应的生命形式繁荣了起来。

cues.en: This is evolution.
cues.zh: 这就是进化。

cues.en: Copy,
cues.zh: 复制、

cues.en: transform,
cues.zh: 改造，

cues.en: and combine.
cues.zh: 再结合。

cues.en: And culture evolves in a similar way, but the elements aren't genes, they're memes,
cues.zh: 文化的进化也是如此，只不过它的基本单元不是基因，而是模因（meme），

cues.en: ideas, behaviors,
cues.zh: 是想法、行为

cues.en: skills.
cues.zh: 和技能。

cues.en: Memes are copied, transformed,
cues.zh: 模因被复制、改造，

cues.en: and combined. And the dominant ideas of our time are the memes that spread the most. This is social evolution.
cues.zh: 再结合。而我们这个时代的主流观念，就是传播最广的模因。这就是社会进化。

cues.en: Copy, transform,
cues.zh: 复制、改造，

cues.en: and combine.
cues.zh: 再结合。

cues.en: It's who we are, it's how we live, and of course, it's how we create.
cues.zh: 这就是我们本身，是我们的生存之道，当然，也是我们创造事物的方式。

cues.en: Our new ideas evolve from the old ones.
cues.zh: 我们的新想法正是从旧想法中进化而来的。

cues.en: But our system of law doesn't acknowledge the derivative nature of creativity.
cues.zh: 但我们的法律体系不承认创造力具有衍生性。

cues.en: Instead, ideas are regarded as property,
cues.zh: 相反，思想被视为财产，

cues.en: as unique and original lots with distinct boundaries.
cues.zh: 是独特原创、边界分明的地块。

cues.en: But ideas aren't so tidy.
cues.zh: 但思想并非如此规整。

cues.en: They're layered, they're interwoven,
cues.zh: 它们层层叠加、相互交织，

cues.en: they're tangled.
cues.zh: 纠缠在一起。

cues.en: And when the system conflicts with the reality,
cues.zh: 当体系与现实发生冲突，

cues.en: the system starts to fail.
cues.zh: 体系就开始失灵。

cues.en: For almost our entire history, ideas were free. The works of Shakespeare, Gutenberg, and Rembrandt could be openly copied and built upon. But the growing dominance of the market economy where the products of our intellectual labors are bought and sold produced an unfortunate side effect. Let's
cues.zh: 纵观我们几乎全部的历史，思想都是自由的。莎士比亚、古腾堡和伦勃朗的作品可以被公开复制并在此基础上再创作。但市场经济的日益主导——我们的智力劳动成果被买卖——产生了一个不幸的副作用。假设

cues.en: say a guy invents a better light bulb. His price needs to cover not just the manufacturing cost, but also the cost of inventing the thing in the first place. Now let's say a competitor starts manufacturing a competing copy.
cues.zh: 有人发明了更好的灯泡。他的定价不仅要覆盖制造成本，还要覆盖最初发明这个东西的成本。现在假设有个竞争对手开始制造仿制竞品。

cues.en: The competitor doesn't need to cover those development costs, so his version can be cheaper. The bottom line, original creations can't compete with the price of copies.
cues.zh: 竞争对手不需要分摊这些研发成本，所以他的版本可以更便宜。结果就是，原创作品在价格上根本拼不过仿制品。

cues.en: In The United States, the introduction of copyrights and patents was intended to address this imbalance.
cues.zh: 在美国，引入版权和专利制度正是为了解决这种不平衡。

cues.en: Copyrights covered media, patents covered inventions.
cues.zh: 版权针对的是媒体作品，专利针对的是发明创造。

cues.en: Both aim to encourage the creation and proliferation
cues.zh: 两者的目的都是为了鼓励新想法的产生

cues.en: of new ideas by providing a brief and limited period of exclusivity,
cues.zh: 与传播，方式是提供一个短暂且有限的独占期，

cues.en: a period where no one else could copy your work. This gave creators a window in which to cover their investments and earn a profit.
cues.zh: 在此期间任何人都不能抄袭你的成果。这给创作者留出了一扇窗口，让他们能收回投资并获得利润。

cues.en: After that, their work entered the public domain where it could spread far and wide and be freely built upon. And it was this that was the goal, a robust public domain, an affordable body of ideas,
cues.zh: 之后，他们的作品进入公共领域，得以广泛传播、自由借鉴。这正是目标所在：一个健全的公共领域，一套人人负担得起的思想、

cues.en: products, arts, entertainment available
cues.zh: 产品、艺术与娱乐内容，

cues.en: to all. The core belief was in the common good, what would benefit everyone.
cues.zh: 向所有人开放。其核心理念是共同利益，即惠及每一个人的东西。

cues.en: But over time, the influence of the market transformed this principle beyond recognition.
cues.zh: 但随着时间推移，市场的影响力让这一原则变得面目全非。

cues.en: Influential thinkers proposed that ideas are a form of property, and this conviction would eventually yield a new term, intellectual
cues.zh: 有影响力的思想家提出，思想也是一种财产，这种观念最终催生了一个新词：知识

cues.en: property.
cues.zh: 产权。

cues.en: This was a meme that would multiply wildly,
cues.zh: 这个观念像模因一样疯狂传播，

cues.en: thanks in part to a quirk of human psychology
cues.zh: 一定程度上得益于人类的一种心理怪癖，

cues.en: known as loss aversion.
cues.zh: 即所谓的“损失厌恶”。

cues.en: Simply put, we hate losing what we've got. People tend to place a much higher value on losses than on gains. So the gains we get from copying the work of others don't make a big impression. But when it's our ideas being copied, we perceive this as a loss and we get territorial.
cues.zh: 简单来说，我们极度讨厌失去已有的东西。比起得到，人们往往更在意失去。因此，借鉴他人作品带来的收获并不会让我们印象深刻。可一旦自己的创意被抄袭，我们就会觉得蒙受了损失，并立刻产生强烈的领地意识。

cues.en: For instance, Disney made extensive use of the public domain. Stories like Snow White, Pinocchio and Alice in Wonderland were all taken from the public domain. But when it came time for the copyright of Disney's early films to expire,
cues.zh: 比如，迪士尼大量利用了公有领域。像《白雪公主》《匹诺曹》和《爱丽丝梦游仙境》这些故事都取自公有领域。但当迪士尼早期电影的版权即将到期时，

cues.en: they lobbied to have the term of copyright extended.
cues.zh: 他们游说延长版权期限。

cues.en: Artist Shepard Fairey has frequently used existing art in his work. This practice came to a head when he was sued by the Associated Press for basing his famous Obama hope poster on their photo. Nonetheless, when it was his imagery used in a piece by Baxter Orr, very threatened to sue.
cues.zh: 艺术家Shepard Fairey经常在其作品中使用现有艺术作品。这种做法在他被美联社起诉时达到顶点，因为他的著名奥巴马“希望”海报是基于他们的照片创作的。然而，当Baxter Orr在一件作品中使用了Fairey的图像时，Fairey威胁要起诉。

cues.en: And lastly, Steve Jobs was sometimes boastful about Apple's history of copying. We have, you know, always been
cues.zh: 最后，Steve Jobs 有时还会吹嘘 Apple 抄袭的历史。你知道的，对于窃取伟大的创意，我们向来

cues.en: shameless about stealing great ideas. But he harbored deep grudges against those who dared to copy Apple. I'm going to destroy Android because it's a stolen product. I'm willing to go thermonuclear
cues.zh: 不知羞耻。但他对那些敢抄 Apple 的人却深恶痛绝。“我要摧毁 Android，因为它是偷来的产品。为了这个我宁愿发动热核

cues.en: war on this.
cues.zh: 战争。”

cues.en: When we copy,
cues.zh: 我们自己抄袭时，

cues.en: we justify it. When others copy,
cues.zh: 就觉得理所当然；别人抄袭时，

cues.en: we vilify it. Most of us have no problem with copying
cues.zh: 我们就严厉谴责。我们大多数人对抄袭都无所谓，

cues.en: as long as we're the ones doing it.
cues.zh: 只要抄的人是我们自己就行。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: with a blind eye toward our own mimicry and propelled by faith in markets and ownership, intellectual property swelled beyond its original scope with broader interpretations of existing laws, new legislation,
cues.zh: 由于我们对自身的模仿行为视而不见，再加上对市场和所有权的盲目信仰，知识产权在原有范围之外不断扩张——对现有法律作更宽泛的解读、出台新立法、

cues.en: new realms of coverage, and alluring rewards.
cues.zh: 开拓新的覆盖领域，还有诱人的回报。

cues.en: In 1981, George Harrison lost a $1,500,000
cues.zh: 1981年，George Harrison输掉了一场150万美元的官司，

cues.en: case for subconsciously
cues.zh: 原因是他在潜意识中

cues.en: copying the duo hit He's So Fine in his ballad My Sweet Lord.
cues.zh: 抄袭了这对组合的热门歌曲He's So Fine，用在了自己的歌谣My Sweet Lord中。

cues.en: Prior to this, plenty of songs sounded much more like other songs without ending up in court. Ray Charles created the prototype for soul music when he based I Got A Woman on the gospel song, It Must Be Jesus.
cues.zh: 在此之前，很多歌曲听起来比这更像别的歌，却从未闹上法庭。Ray Charles以福音歌曲It Must Be Jesus为蓝本创作了I Got A Woman，由此创造了灵魂乐的雏形。

cues.en: Starting in the late nineties, a series of new copyright laws and regulations began to be introduced,
cues.zh: 从90年代末开始，一系列新的版权法规相继出台，

cues.en: and many more are in the works. The most ambitious in scope are trade agreements.
cues.zh: 而且还有更多在筹备中。其中涉及范围最广的是贸易协定。

cues.en: Because these are treaties and not laws, they can be negotiated in secret with no public inputs and no congressional approval.
cues.zh: 因为它们是条约而非法律，所以可以完全闭门谈判，既不需要公众参与，也无需国会批准。

cues.en: ACTA was signed by president Obama,
cues.zh: ACTA 由奥巴马总统签署生效，

cues.en: and the Trans Pacific Partnership Agreement, currently being written in secret, aims to spread even stronger US style protections around the world. Of course, when The United States itself was a developing economy, it refused to sign treaties and had no protection for foreign creators.
cues.zh: 而目前正在秘密起草的《跨太平洋伙伴关系协定》（TPP），更旨在向全球推广更严苛的美式版权保护。当然，当年美国自己还是发展中经济体时，也是拒绝签署条约，对外国创作者毫无保护可言的。

cues.en: Charles Dickens famously complained about America's bustling book piracy market, calling it a horrible thing that scoundrel booksellers
cues.zh: 查尔斯·狄更斯曾著名地抱怨美国繁荣的图书盗版市场，称其为一桩可怕的事，无赖书商

cues.en: should grow rich.
cues.zh: 竟然因此致富。

cues.en: Patent coverage made the leap from physical inventions to virtual ones, most notably software.
cues.zh: 专利保护范围从实体发明跨越到了虚拟发明，其中最显著的是软件。

cues.en: But this is not a natural transition.
cues.zh: 但这并非自然而然的转变。

cues.en: A patent is a blueprint for how to make an invention.
cues.zh: 专利是指导如何制造发明的蓝图。

cues.en: Software patents are are more like a loose description of what something would be like if it actually was invented.
cues.zh: 软件专利更像是对于某物如果真被发明出来会是什么样的一种宽泛描述。

cues.en: Software patents are written in the broadest possible language to get the broadest possible protection.
cues.zh: 软件专利的措辞往往尽可能宽泛，好获得最大范围的保护。

cues.en: The vagueness of these terms can sometimes reach absurd levels.
cues.zh: 这种用词的含糊程度有时简直到了荒谬的地步。

cues.en: For example, information
cues.zh: 比如，“信息

cues.en: machine which covers anything computer like or material object which covers pretty much anything.
cues.zh: 机器”，能涵盖任何类似计算机的东西；或者“实体”，几乎能指代世间万物。

cues.en: The fuzziness of software patents boundaries has turned the smartphone industry into one giant turf war.
cues.zh: 软件专利边界的模糊性，把智能手机行业变成了一场巨大的地盘争夺战。

cues.en: Sixty two percent of all patent lawsuits are now over software.
cues.zh: 如今，有 62% 的专利诉讼都针对软件。

cues.en: The estimated wealth lost is $500,000,000,000.
cues.zh: 估计损失财富达 5000 亿美元。

cues.en: The expanding reach of intellectual property has introduced more and more possibilities
cues.zh: 知识产权不断扩大的覆盖范围带来了越来越多的可能性，

cues.en: for opportunistic
cues.zh: 为投机性的

cues.en: litigation.
cues.zh: 诉讼提供了机会。

cues.en: Suing to make a buck. Two new species evolved whose entire business model is lawsuits.
cues.zh: 靠起诉赚钱。两个新物种进化出来，其全部商业模式就是打官司。

cues.en: Sample trolls and patent trolls.
cues.zh: 样本钓饵和专利钓饵。

cues.en: These are corporations that don't actually produce anything.
cues.zh: 这些公司实际上不生产任何东西。

cues.en: They acquire a library of intellectual property rights, then litigate to earn profits. And because legal defense is hundreds of thousands of dollars in copyright cases and millions in patents,
cues.zh: 他们获取一批知识产权，然后通过诉讼获利。而且，由于版权案件的法律辩护费用高达数十万美元，专利案件高达数百万美元，

cues.en: their targets are usually highly motivated to settle out of court.
cues.zh: 他们的目标通常非常有动力在庭外和解。

cues.en: The most famous sample troll is Bridgeport Music, which has filed hundreds of lawsuits. In 2005, they scored an influential court decision over this two second sample.
cues.zh: 最著名的采样流氓当属 Bridgeport Music，他们提起了数百起诉讼。2005 年，他们凭借这段两秒钟的采样，赢得了一场极具影响力的判决。

cues.en: That's it. And not only was the sample short, it was virtually unrecognizable.
cues.zh: 就这么短。而且这采样不仅短，还几乎听不出来原貌。

cues.en: This verdict essentially rendered any kind of sampling, no matter how small, infringing.
cues.zh: 这项判决实际上将任何形式的采样，无论多微小，都定性为侵权。

cues.en: The sample heavy musical collages of hip hop's golden age are now impossibly expensive to create. Now
cues.zh: 如今，要想重现嘻哈黄金时代那种大量使用采样的音乐拼贴，成本已经高到令人无法承受。现在

cues.en: patent trolls are most common back in that troubled realm of software,
cues.zh: 专利流氓在软件这个麻烦不断的领域里最为猖獗，

cues.en: and perhaps the most inexplicable
cues.zh: 而其中最让人匪夷所思的，

cues.en: case is that of Paul Allen. He's one of the founders of Microsoft. He's a billionaire. He's an esteemed philanthropist who's pledged to give away much of his fortune, and he claims basic web features like related links, alerts, and recommendations
cues.zh: 莫过于 Paul Allen 的案子。他是 Microsoft 的创始人之一，是个亿万富翁，还是一位声名显赫、承诺捐出大部分财产的慈善家，可他却声称拥有相关链接、提醒和推荐等基础 Web 功能的专利

cues.en: were invented by his long defunct company.
cues.zh: 是他的那家早已倒闭的公司发明的。

cues.en: So the self proclaimed idea man sued pretty much all of Silicon Valley in 2010
cues.zh: 于是这位自封的创意家在2010年几乎把整个硅谷都告上了法庭

cues.en: and he did this despite no lack of fame or fortune.
cues.zh: 而他这么做，明明既不缺名也不缺利。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: to recap, the full picture looks like this. We believe that ideas are property and we're excessively territorial
cues.zh: 回顾一下，整幅图景是这样的。我们相信创意是财产，而且领地意识极强

cues.en: when we feel that property belongs to us.
cues.zh: 一旦觉得这份财产属于自己。

cues.en: Our laws then indulge this bias with ever broadening protections
cues.zh: 我们的法律便纵容这种偏见，保护范围越来越宽

cues.en: and massive rewards.
cues.zh: 回报也越来越丰厚。

cues.en: Meanwhile, huge legal fees encourage defendants to pay up and settle out of court.
cues.zh: 与此同时，高昂的诉讼费迫使被告不得不花钱和解。

cues.en: It's a discouraging scenario and it begs the question,
cues.zh: 这很让人沮丧，也引发了一个问题：

cues.en: what now?
cues.zh: 我们现在该怎么办？

cues.en: The belief in intellectual property has grown so dominant,
cues.zh: 人们对知识产权的笃信已经占据了主导地位，

cues.en: it's pushed the original intent of copyrights
cues.zh: 以至于版权的最初意图

cues.en: and patents out of the public consciousness.
cues.zh: 以及专利都被公众抛在脑后了。

cues.en: But that original purpose is still right there in plain sight. The copyright act of 1790 is entitled an act for the encouragement of learning.
cues.zh: 但那个最初的宗旨依然清晰可见：1790年的《版权法》其全称正是《促进学习法》。

cues.en: The patent act is to promote the progress of useful arts.
cues.zh: 专利法的目的是促进实用技艺的进步。

cues.en: The exclusive rights these acts introduced were a compromise for a greater purpose.
cues.zh: 这些法案引入的专有权是为了更宏大目标而做的妥协。

cues.en: The intent was to better the lives of everyone by incentivizing creativity and producing a rich public domain,
cues.zh: 其本意是通过激励创造力、缔造丰富的公共领域来改善所有人的生活，

cues.en: a shared pool of knowledge open to all.
cues.zh: 一个向所有人开放的共享知识池。

cues.en: But exclusive rights themselves came to be considered the point, so they were strengthened and expanded
cues.zh: 但专有权本身逐渐被当成了目的，于是被不断加强和扩张，

cues.en: and the result hasn't been more progress or more learning, it's been more squabbling and more abuse.
cues.zh: 结果并没有带来更多进步或更多学习，而是更多的争执和更多的滥用。

cues.en: We live in an age with daunting problems.
cues.zh: 我们生活在一个难题丛生的时代。

cues.en: We need the best ideas possible,
cues.zh: 我们需要尽可能优秀的思想，

cues.en: we need them now, we need them to spread fast.
cues.zh: 我们现在就需要，且需要它们快速传播。

cues.en: The common good is a meme that was overwhelmed
cues.zh: “公益”曾是一个被知识产权

cues.en: by intellectual property.
cues.zh: 所淹没的模因。

cues.en: It needs to spread again. If the meme prospers,
cues.zh: 它需要再次传播开来。如果这个模因繁荣起来，

cues.en: our laws, our norms, our society,
cues.zh: 我们的法律、规范、社会，

cues.en: they all transform.
cues.zh: 都将随之转变。

cues.en: That's social evolution
cues.zh: 这就是社会进化。

cues.en: It's not up to governments,
cues.zh: 这不取决于政府，

cues.en: corporations,
cues.zh: 不取决于企业，

cues.en: or lawyers.
cues.zh: 也不取决于律师。

cues.en: It's up
cues.zh: 它取决于

cues.en: to us.
cues.zh: 我们自己。
